cls: Vaccine - recombinant hepatitis B surface antigen (active immunization)
quick: 1 mL (20 mcg HBsAg) IM at 0, 1, and 6 months (3-dose series); Heplisav-B is a 2-dose adult schedule at 0 and 1 month
Not contraindicated; recommended for at-risk and HBsAg-screened pregnant women
Safe; may be given to breastfeeding women
Dialysis/CKD patients need higher-dose (40 mcg) formulations/schedules and antibody monitoring
Not contraindicated; recommended in chronic liver disease
Anti-HBs titer in high-risk groups (dialysis, healthcare workers, infants of HBsAg+ mothers)
summary: Hepatitis B vaccine is a recombinant vaccine containing hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) produced in yeast, used for active immunization against all subtypes of hepatitis B virus. It induces protective anti-HBs antibodies. It is given intramuscularly in a multi-dose series (commonly 0, 1, 6 months) and is recommended universally for infants and for at-risk adults. It is contraindicated in those with severe allergy to a prior dose or to vaccine components, including yeast.
indications: Active immunization against infection by all known subtypes of hepatitis B virus
Universal infant immunization (including a birth dose, ideally within 24 hours of birth)
Immunization of unvaccinated children, adolescents, and at-risk or all adults
High-risk groups: healthcare workers, dialysis/CKD patients, household and sexual contacts of HBsAg-positive persons, people who inject drugs, men who have sex with men, travelers to endemic areas

dosage.n: Heplisav-B alternative: 2 doses at 0 and 1 month
Birth dose within 24 h; complete series per national schedule

dosage.d: Vaccine 0.5 mL (10 mcg) PLUS hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG) at separate sites
dosage.t: Within 12 h of birth, then complete series
dosage.n: Check anti-HBs and HBsAg at 9-12 months
Monitor anti-HBs; give booster if titer falls

admin: Administer intramuscularly - deltoid in adults/children, anterolateral thigh in infants; do NOT give in the gluteus (reduced response) or intradermally
Shake the vial/syringe well before use to obtain a uniform suspension
Do not mix in the same syringe with other vaccines; if HBIG is co-administered, use a separate site
Complete the full series for durable protection; the third dose is critical for long-term immunity
Have epinephrine available for the rare event of anaphylaxis; observe after vaccination
moa: The vaccine contains recombinant hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) expressed in yeast and adsorbed onto an adjuvant (typically aluminum salt; Heplisav-B uses a CpG adjuvant). It induces a humoral immune response producing anti-HBs antibodies that neutralize hepatitis B virus. An anti-HBs level >=10 mIU/mL after vaccination is considered protective.

absolute: Severe allergic reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis) after a previous dose of any hepatitis B-containing vaccine
Severe allergic reaction to any vaccine component, including yeast (HBsAg is yeast-derived)
relative: Moderate or severe acute illness with or without fever (defer until recovery)
Hypersensitivity to latex (some prefilled syringe tip caps)

preg: Hepatitis B vaccine is not contraindicated in pregnancy. It contains non-infectious recombinant antigen and is recommended for pregnant women at risk of HBV infection, and all pregnant women should be screened for HBsAg. (Note: Heplisav-B has limited pregnancy data; conventional recombinant vaccines are preferred during pregnancy.) The benefit of preventing maternal and perinatal HBV infection generally outweighs theoretical risks.
lact: Hepatitis B vaccine can be given to breastfeeding women; it poses no risk to the breastfed infant and does not affect the safety of breastfeeding for mother or child.
renal: Patients with chronic kidney disease and those on dialysis respond less well and require higher-dose formulations/additional doses (e.g., 40 mcg) and post-vaccination anti-HBs testing, with booster doses if titers fall below the protective threshold.
hepatic: Not contraindicated; hepatitis B vaccination is specifically recommended for patients with chronic liver disease to prevent superimposed HBV infection.

moderate: Immunosuppressive therapy or immunodeficiency (corticosteroids, chemotherapy, biologics) may blunt the antibody response - check anti-HBs and consider revaccination
minor: May be co-administered with other vaccines and with hepatitis B immunoglobulin (HBIG) using separate sites and syringes without impairing efficacy
interactions.diagnostics: Transient low-level HBsAg may be detectable in blood for days after vaccination, potentially causing a false-positive HBsAg test

rare: Reports of Guillain-Barre syndrome (causal link not established)
emergency: Anaphylaxis (difficulty breathing, swelling, hypotension) within minutes to hours of vaccination

monitoring: Observe for immediate hypersensitivity/syncope after administration
Post-vaccination anti-HBs titer (1-2 months after the last dose) in high-risk groups: healthcare workers, dialysis patients, infants of HBsAg-positive mothers, immunocompromised
Booster doses guided by anti-HBs levels in dialysis/immunocompromised patients
counsel: Completing all doses in the series is essential for lasting protection - keep your follow-up appointments
Mild soreness at the injection site, tiredness, or a low fever are common and usually settle within a day or two
Tell the vaccinator about any severe allergy to a previous hepatitis B vaccine or to yeast
Sit or lie down during and after the injection if you tend to feel faint
Seek immediate help for difficulty breathing, swelling of the face/throat, or hives shortly after vaccination
pk: Antibody (anti-HBs) response develops over weeks after each dose
Protective anti-HBs titers (>=10 mIU/mL) typically achieved 1-2 months after the final dose
Not applicable (vaccine induces active immunity rather than having a drug half-life)
Long-lasting immune memory; protection persists for many years (often lifelong) in immunocompetent responders
Store at 2-8 C; do NOT freeze (freezing destroys the vaccine); protect from light
pearls: Universal infant vaccination with a birth dose (within 24 h) is the cornerstone of HBV elimination; HBsAg-positive mothers' newborns also need HBIG
Contraindicated in severe allergy to a prior dose or to any component including YEAST (HBsAg is produced in yeast)
Dialysis and immunocompromised patients need higher antigen doses and anti-HBs monitoring with boosters
A protective response is an anti-HBs level >=10 mIU/mL; non-responders may be offered a repeat series
missed: If a dose in the series is delayed or missed, resume the series as soon as possible - do NOT restart from the beginning. Give the remaining dose(s) maintaining the minimum required intervals between doses; an interrupted schedule does not require restarting.
overdose: Vaccine overdose is not clinically meaningful; inadvertent administration of an extra dose is not harmful. Manage any local or systemic reaction symptomatically.
